verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission of NASA's Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'NASA’s Artemis II is the first crewed mission of the Artemis program'; R2: 'Coming more than three years after the uncrewed Artemis I test flight, Artemis II will mark the first time humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state or imply Artemis II is the first crewed Artemis mission, following uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to take approximately four to five days to reach the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly a four-day journey to the far side of the moon'; R9: 'reach the moon in five days'; R4: 'day six of the mission'; R2: 'three days to get to the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe ~3-5 day translunar coast after initial Earth orbit, approximating 4-5 days total from launch to lunar vicinity.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II will enter the lunar vicinity around day five.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R9: 'reach the moon in five days'; R7: 'On day five, the Orion will enter the lunar sphere of influence'; R4: 'day six of the mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources vary slightly between day 5 and 6 for entering lunar vicinity, but 'around day five' is broadly supported.

verifications.claim: The total mission duration of Artemis II is roughly 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'From launch the evening of April 1 to splashdown on April 10, the mission is slated to last about nine and a half days'; R2: 'more than 600,000-mile, 10-day journey'; R3: 'approximately 10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Nearly all sources describe the mission as ~10 days total.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will fly around the moon before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the plan is to loop around it'; R2: 'lunar flyby'; R4: 'whip around the lunar far side'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm a flyby looping around the moon without landing or orbiting.

verifications.claim: Artemis II involves crewed travel to the far side of the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'getting an unprecedented view of the far side of the moon'; R2: 'fly by the far side of the moon'; R5: 'trip around the “dark side of the moon”'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe travel to/around the far side.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft will travel at speeds up to 24,500 mph (39,400 km/h) to escape Earth's gravity before slowing down and being pulled in by the Moon's gravity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Escape velocity...is 24,500 miles per hour...slowed to just 3,400 mph...gravitational pull of the moon will take over'; R5: 'nearly 24,000 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: R4 matches speed exactly for escape and describes deceleration then lunar gravity pull.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will take the crew 252,000 miles from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'farthest distance humans have ever traveled from Earth: 252,000 miles'; R7: 'about 252,000 miles into space'
verifications.reasoning: Exact distance cited in sources for max distance from Earth.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will set a record for the farthest humans have traveled into space.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'expected to travel farther from Earth than anyone before them'; R3: 'expected to send the crew farther from Earth than any previous human mission'; R4: 'farther from Earth than any person has ever ventured'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources state it will break the Apollo record.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will make one pass around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'make one pass around the moon'; R2: 'fly by the far side...circle it for a return'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe a single flyby/pass around the moon.

verifications.claim: The return trip to Earth for Artemis II is expected to take another three to four days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'another four days back to Earth'; R2: 'three-day return trip'; R4: 'homeward trip will take in excess of 96 hours'; R5: 'up to four days'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe 3-4 day return, matching 'another three to four days'.

verifications.claim: The CBS News update and NASA official blog note that the projected Artemis II mission timeline is scheduled for April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 (CBS News): dated 'April 1, 2026' with live launch updates; R3 (NASA blog): 'Live launch day updates...April 1, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: R1 (CBS) and R3 (NASA blog) are dated April 2026 and cover the launch timeline/schedule.
